q: A provider hangs and never answers. Your API has 4 slots and no timeout. Four checkouts are waiting. What happens to a user who logs in (login never calls the provider)?
options: Login works, because it does not use the provider
Login fails, because every slot is held by a stuck checkout
Login works but is slow
Login waits until the provider answers
why: Each stuck call holds a slot. When all slots are held, the login finds none, even though it never needed the provider. A timeout frees the slot (in the real run, login got 503 without a timeout and 200 with one).

q: Three layers each try a failing call 3 times. How many calls reach the bottom, and what is the usual rule?
options: 9 calls. Retry at every layer to be safe
27 calls. Retry at one layer only
3 calls. Layers do not add up
27 calls. Add more tries at the bottom
why: 3 x 3 x 3 = 27, and 5 layers give 243. Retries multiply across layers, so retry at one layer, the one directly above the failing system, with a small number of tries.

q: Which failure is worth retrying (and the call is safe to repeat)?
options: 400, the data is wrong
404, the item does not exist
A timeout or a 503
401, the login is wrong
why: A timeout or a 503 can pass by itself. A 400, 401 or 404 will fail again every time, so a retry only adds load.

q: 1000 clients fail at the same moment. They retry with waits that double (100, 200, 400 ms) and no random part. What does the server see?
options: A steady stream
A wall of 1000 calls in each round
Half the calls, because the waits grow
No retries, because backoff stops them
why: Backoff makes the retries rarer but every client waits the same time, so they stay together. Jitter gives each client a random wait, which spreads the calls (115 in the busiest 10 ms slot against 1000 in the real run).

q: In full jitter, with a base of 100 ms, what is the wait before the retry at attempt 3 when random() gives 0.5 (no cap reached)?
options: 800 ms
400 ms
50 ms
200 ms
why: The ceiling is 100 x 2 to the power of 3 = 800 ms. The wait is random() x ceiling = 0.5 x 800 = 400 ms.

q: A circuit breaker is open and its cooldown is over. It is now half open. What does it do?
options: Closes at once
Lets every call through to see what happens
Lets one test call through. A good result closes it, a bad one opens it again
Stays open until someone restarts it
why: Half open sends one test call. If it works the breaker closes and the failure count resets. If it fails the breaker opens again and the cooldown restarts.
